ben_support: Heads-up — enterprise customer 'AcmeCorp' hit a big latency spike and huge token billing yesterday. They say requests targeting us-west kept being routed to eu-west and falling back to cheaper model variants. Can SRE/infra take a look?

marta_sre: Oof. Do we have a trace ID or a reproducible request?

ben_support: Trace: tracex-8f3b. Repro (sanitized):
```
curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED' \
  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?region=us-west' \
  -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
```
Response headers I captured: `x-served-region: eu-west-1`, `x-latency-ms: 482`, status 200. Customer expected ~40ms. Billing shows per-token costs bumped since route crossed zones.

dinesh_engineer: Looking at traces — requests had client-IP -> us-west edge, but smart-routing forwarded to eu-west pool because the us-west health-check for the preferred pool flipped to UNHEALTHY at ~2026-03-14T10:02Z. We show a burst of heartbeat failures from the us-west probe aggregator.

carla_ops: I pulled probe logs for the agent fleet in us-west. There's a restart around the same time, agent re-registered with a tag `region=eu-west-1` (!!!) due to fallback when ENV_REGION was empty. Log excerpt:
```
[10:01:58] probe-agent: starting, ENV_REGION=
[10:01:59] probe-agent: failed to read metadata -> using cloud-metadata fallback
[10:02:01] probe-agent: metadata gave availability_zone=eu-west-1b -> registering as region=eu-west-1
[10:02:03] heartbeat: sent, status=PASS
```

marta_sre: That would definitely explain routing — health index thinks us-west capacity = 0 so policy routes to eu-west. Why did ENV_REGION go blank? Any deploys or config pushes?

dinesh_engineer: There's a config rollout last night for the probe container image that included a new startup path for metadata; it added a retry backoff that accidentally swallowed initial metadata reads. If the first metadata call times out it falls back to cloud metadata which in the multicloud testbed returned a stale AZ mapping (eu-west) for some ephemeral instances.

ben_support: Customer is asking for repro steps and mitigation we did. Can we reproduce locally or show fix?

carla_ops: Repro steps I used: 1) spin up a probe container with ENV_REGION unset, 2) mock cloud-metadata to return eu-west az, 3) kill / restart agent quickly so bootstrap happens during metadata outage. That reproduces mis-registration every time.

marta_sre: Immediate mitigation applied: pinned routing to prefer X-Client-Region header when health score difference < 20% and added a short-circuit to ignore agent registrations that flip zone within 30s of start. Also forced a rollout to revert probe-image to previous tag for the affected autoscaling group. Deploy-bot created incident INC-20260314-77.

deploy-bot: Incident INC-20260314-77 created and assigned to eng-sre. Priority: P2.

tim_product: Thanks — customer notified with workaround (force region via header) and billing team issued a one-time adjustment. Please confirm when fixed so I can close the ticket.

dinesh_engineer: We've pushed a patch to the probe startup: require stable metadata for 10s before registering and log a clear WARN if fallback used. Also added a health-check hysteresis of 2 probes (was 1). Rolling to us-west pool now (rolling restart, 25% at a time).

carla_ops: Post-rollout checks: us-west health index returned to normal within ~4m, routing reverted, median p50 latency for AcmeCorp back to 38ms. Billing spike contained; ops recorded the adjustment.

marta_sre: Follow-ups: 1) postmortem in #postmortems, 2) increase probe sample rate by 2x for edge pools, 3) add alert if more than 3 agents in a region start with ENV_REGION unset in 5m. I'll file the tasks.

ben_support: Perfect — I've told the customer the root cause, workaround, and fix. They'll re-open if they see anything else. Thanks all. :heart:
